after: An image’s `width` and `height` help the browser leave space before the picture loads. The supplied ridge picture is 640 pixels wide and 320 tall. That makes it twice as wide as it is tall.
`loading="lazy"` lets the browser wait to load a picture that is far down the page. It can save loading work. Use it for a later picture, not the main picture people need to see straight away.

This example reserves the ridge picture’s shape. ```html ``` `src` names the supplied picture. `alt` describes it. `width` and `height` give its size and shape. `loading="lazy"` requests later loading when appropriate.
Changing lazy to eager asks for normal immediate loading. It does not change width or height. When the image loads and how much space it needs are separate settings.
